'''Judith''' ('''Judy''') '''Green''' (born 1943)<ref>Birth year from [http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2008054696.html Library of Congress catalog entry], retrieved 2018-12-07.</ref> is an American [[logician]] and [[History of mathematics|historian of mathematics]] who studies [[Timeline of women in mathematics|women in mathematics]].{{r|profile}} She is a founding member of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]];{{r|awm|change}} she has also served as its vice president, and as the vice president of the [[American Association of University Professors]].{{r|profile}}

==Education and career==
Green earned her bachelor's degree at [[Cornell University]].
She completed a master's degree at [[Yale University]],
and a Ph.D. at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]].{{r|profile}}
Her dissertation, supervised by [[Carol Karp]] and finished in 1972, was
''Consistency Properties for Uncountable Finite-Quantifier Languages''.{{r|mgp}}

Green was elected an [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]] Member at Large in 1975 and served for three years until 1977.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-28 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref> She belonged to the faculty of [[Rutgers University]] before moving to [[Marymount University]] in 1989. After retiring from Marymount in 2007, she became a volunteer at the [[National Museum of American History]].{{r|profile}}

==Book==
With [[Jeanne LaDuke]], she wrote ''[[Pioneering Women in American Mathematics|Pioneering Women in American Mathematics: The Pre-1940 PhD’s]]'' ([[American Mathematical Society]] and [[London Mathematical Society]], 2009). This was a biographical study of the first women in the U.S. to earn doctorates in mathematics.{{r|pwam}}

==Recognition==
She is part of the 2019 class of fellows of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/|title=2019 Class of AWM Fellows|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|access-date=2019-01-08}}</ref>
